title: MasakhaNER 2.0 - Named Entity Recognition for African Languages
description: Span-level named entity recognition for African-language text, following the MasakhaNER 2.0 annotation scheme (Adelani et al., EMNLP 2022): the largest human-annotated NER dataset for African languages, covering 20 languages such as Swahili, Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo, Nigerian-Pidgin and isiZulu. Native-speaker annotators, trained on the MUC-6 guidelines, highlight four entity types - Person (PER), Organization (ORG), Location (LOC) and Date & Time (DATE) - then confirm the overall entity composition of the sentence. Illustrative sample items include an English gloss for reference only; real annotation is done by native speakers without glosses.
overview: MasakhaNER 2.0 is the largest human-annotated named entity recognition dataset for African languages, covering 20 of them. Adelani and colleagues built it through the Masakhane community and published it at EMNLP 2022.

The text is mostly local news, with some sentences from the MAFAND-MT translation corpus. Native speakers annotated four entity types — person (PER), location (LOC), organization (ORG), and date and time (DATE) — following the MUC-6 named-entity guidelines. The DATE type replaces CoNLL's MISC, which the authors found caused disagreement.

Each language was annotated by three native speakers with a language coordinator who trained them and adjudicated disagreements; annotators were paid, and agreement was measured with Fleiss' kappa. Data is split 70/10/20 into train, development, and test.

The Potato config below reproduces the task with a span scheme for the four entity types plus a check for whether a sentence contains entities. Use it to extend MasakhaNER to a new language or to annotate NER in low-resource text.
